concerns.recommendation: Flag to Baird as a likely GEM-only/unconfirmed entity. Do not treat as a confirmed operating gas pipeline pending a stronger source; consider whether it should be retired, merged into an existing roster row, or downgraded to 'unconfirmed'.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's own gem.wiki page for this pipeline carries exactly one citation: 'World Energy Atlas, Petroleum Economist, 2001' — a print atlas with no URL, unverifiable and (per standing rules) not citable regardless. wiki_citations.json independently confirms zero harvestable citations for this row. So the sheet has never had an independently checkable source for this entity at all. I then tried to independently confirm the pipeline via the SAME authoritative source that underpins nearly every other pipeline in this 30-row Libya gas roster: OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (p.75; live opec.org copy 301-redirects to the homepage, retrieved instead via the Wayback Machine capture and confirmed with curl+pdftotext, since url_verifier's substring screen cannot read binary PDF byte streams — same documented false-negative as sibling row P1869). That single OPEC table lists 21 named Libyan gas pipelines and its length/diameter/capacity figures match — essentially exactly, after mi->km and 1,000 scm/yr->bcm/y conversion — 21 of the ~30 pipelines on this project's in-scope roster: Wafa/Mellitah=P0484, Bahr Assalam/Mellitah=P1855/P6713, Mellitah/Gela=P0439 (Greenstream), Intesar/Brega=P1856 (207mi=333km, 42in, 42,480,884 th.scm/yr=42.48 bcm/y — exact match to P1856's cap=42.48), 103D/103A=P1857, Bu-Attifel/Intesar=P1858/P6714, Bouri/Bahr Assalam=P1859/P6709, Waha/Nasser=P1860, Faregh/Intesar=P1861, Brega/Benghazi=P1862, Brega/Khoms=P1863, Khoms/Tripoli=P1864, Tripoli/Mellitah=P1865, Nasser/Brega=P1866, Attahaddy/km-91.5=P1867, Km-81.5/Brega=P1868, Raguba/km-110=P1869, Intesar/Sahel=P1870, Sahel/km-81.5=P1871, Km-91.5/Brega=P1872, Jakhira/Intesar=P1873. This is clearly the (or a) primary data backbone GEM drew this roster from. Crucially, THERE IS NO 'Defa' ENTRY ANYWHERE IN THIS TABLE — not under any of the Libya rows in Table 4.10 (gas), and I also checked Table 4.9 'Crude oil pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (pp.71-72) in the same document in case Defa's line was misclassified as oil — it is also absent there (that table's Libya section lists Sarir/Tobruk, Messla/Amal, Nasser/Al-Brayqah, Amal/Ras Lanuf, Aseida/Ras Lanuf, etc., but no Defa route of any kind). P0482 is one of only a handful of roster rows (alongside P0483 Libya Coastal [a rollup, expected], P3987, P3988, P6705, P1789) missing from this table, and it is distinctive in that its Diameter and Capacity are BOTH still blank in the mainsheet — unlike every OPEC-sourced row, which has all three of length/diameter/capacity populated from that table. Separately, I confirmed 'Defa' IS a real place-name in Libya's Sirte Basin: two Wikipedia geology articles ('Zelten oil field' and 'Raguba field'), both citing a USGS Sirte Basin Province assessment and an academic paper (Belazi, 'The geology of the Nafoora oil field, Sirte basin, Libya', Journal of Petroleum Geology v.12, 1989), describe Defa as one of the Sirte Basin's 'giant oil fields' in the north-center trend, sometimes styled jointly as 'Defa-Waha field' — so the field itself is not invented. But no source found ties Defa to Brega by a dedicated 299km gas line. The only named 'Defa' pipeline I could find anywhere is on Wikipedia's 'Ras Lanuf' article, which twice describes a 'Defa-Ra's Lanuf' OIL pipeline (~251km) — a different commodity and a different endpoint than GEM records — but that specific claim's own citation is Theodora.com/pipelines, a source this project blocklists as an unreliable tertiary aggregator, and it is NOT corroborated by the OPEC table either, so I cannot treat it as confirmation of anything, only as a hint that if a real 'Defa' pipeline exists in the literature at all, everything else about it (commodity, endpoint) contradicts GEM's P0482 record. Net: I could not independently confirm P0482 as a real, distinct, operating 299km Defa-to-Brega GAS pipeline from any source — GEM's own citation is unverifiable, the authoritative OPEC dataset that backstops almost this entire roster is silent on it (in both its gas AND oil tables), and the one 'Defa' pipeline name that does surface in the wider literature points to a different route and commodity, sourced from a source this project excludes. This meets the sweep's 'GEM-only entity' flag criteria.

concerns.researcher_notes: Checked the sheet's own cited source first: wiki_citations.json lists exactly one reference for this page, OPEC's 'Annual Statistics Bulletin' 2012 PDF (opec.org/.../ASB2012.pdf). Verified live (url_verifier: 200, contains 'Libya') but it is a generic country-level statistics bulletin — it does NOT name '103D-103A', '103D', '103A', Zueitina, or any specific pipeline (verifier FAILs on token '103'). Per the standing rule, a row whose only cited support is a generic/aggregate source that doesn't name the pipeline is itself an existence flag, so I escalated to independent open-web research. Findings: (1) 'Intisar A' and 'Intisar D' (a.k.a. field 103A / 103D, from the original Esso-era 'Concession 103' numbering, Sirte Basin) are real, well-documented oil/gas reef fields — confirmed independently via OSTI.gov (a 1970 SPE/JPT-derived abstract: 'Intisar A and D fields on Occidental's Concession 103... located 220 miles south of Benghazi... 15 miles apart') and corroborated by multiple paywalled academic sources found in search snippets (OnePetro, ScienceDirect, ResearchGate — all 403'd on direct fetch, so not cited, but consistent with the OSTI account). (2) Zueitina Oil Company (GEM's listed Operator) is confirmed as the CURRENT real-world operator actively working gas infrastructure specifically at 'Field 103D': a Libya Herald article dated Feb 2026 reports Zueitina Oil Co meeting with US-based BlueVee Energy on H2S gas treatment / 'Gas Cap Blowdown project' technology 'for Field 103D' (verified live, contains 'Zueitina' and '103D' and 'BlueVee'). This independently supports both the Operator value and that 103D is an active gas site today (broadly consistent with Status=operating), but it is about gas processing AT the field, not about a pipeline BETWEEN 103D and 103A. (3) I found NO source, after multiple targeted searches (direct '103D-103A' pipeline queries, 'Zueitina Field 103D OR 103A gas pipeline km', Intisar+concession+103 queries), that names or documents this specific pipeline segment, its 41km length, 40in diameter, or 17.84 bcm/y capacity — those figures are corroborated nowhere outside GEM/the sheet's unhelpful OPEC citation. Given the two fields are real, ~15 miles (~24km) apart, and part of one integrated Occidental/Zueitina-operated production complex, an internal gas gathering/transfer line between them is entirely plausible from an engineering standpoint (this whole 30-pipeline batch is full of similar internal field-to-field/km-marker gathering lines), but plausibility is not the same as confirmation. Recommend downgrading confidence pending a dedicated source (NOC concession pipeline register, EPSA filing, or Zueitina/OMV technical report) rather than treating as confirmed on current sourcing. No duplicate found against the 30-pipeline roster (no other row uses 103A/103D or Intisar naming) and no classification issue beyond the field's own internal-gathering character, which matches the pattern of several other rows in this same batch (e.g. Km-81.5-Brega, Raguba-Km-110) and is not unique to P1857.

concerns.recommendation: Flag for possible retirement/merge or a hard second-source search before keeping any values; do not add refs on the strength of the current citation.
concerns.researcher_notes: The gem.wiki page's ONLY reference (cite_note-1) is 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75' -> https://www.opec.org/opec_web/static_files_project/media/downloads/publications/ASB2012.pdf. Ran url_verifier with expected token 'Waha': FAIL — 200 but missing expected. Manually fetched the URL directly (urllib + curl, distinct UAs): it now resolves to the generic OPEC.org homepage/nav shell (title 'Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries', full of menu text like 'About Us / Member Countries / Libya / Nigeria...'), NOT the actual 2012 Annual Statistical Bulletin PDF — the file path is dead/moved (soft-404, HTTP 200 but wrong content, Content-Type text/html). Even setting the dead-link problem aside, the OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin is a country-level aggregate reserves/production/trade tables publication — it has never itemized named internal Libyan gas-gathering pipeline segments like 'Waha-Nasser', so it would not have supported this specific claim even when live. Checked wiki_citations.json for the other 29 in-scope rows: this EXACT same ASB2012.pdf URL is reused verbatim as the sole citation on at least 10 sibling pages (P1859, P1861, P1866, P1867, P1868, P1869, P1870, P1871, P1872, and P1860 itself) — confirming it is a boilerplate/generic citation pasted across a whole cluster of Sirte Basin internal segment pipelines, not evidence specific to any one of them. Open-web search (English and Arabic) for 'Waha-Nasser gas pipeline' returns only gem.wiki itself and its mirrors/aggregators; nothing independent names a pipeline called 'Waha-Nasser'. Independently confirmed both endpoints are real, distinct entities: Waha field is operated by Waha Oil Co (NOC/ConocoPhillips/TotalEnergies/Hess JV), while Nasser field (formerly Zelten, Libya's first major oil field, discovered 1959) is ~169 km south of Brega and is operated by Sirte Oil Co, a DIFFERENT NOC subsidiary (offshore-technology.com field profile, Wikipedia Zelten oil field, globalsecurity.org Libya petrol background) -- i.e. current Operator/Owner values (Waha Oil Co / NOC+ConocoPhillips+TotalEnergies+Hess) describe the Waha-side JV only and may not be the right attribution if this pipeline genuinely runs to Nasser field's Sirte-Oil-operated infrastructure. One WebSearch AI-summary claimed globalsecurity.org lists 'Defa-Nasser; Nasser-Hatiba; Nasser(Zelten)-Marsa el Brega; Waha-Es Sider' as Libya's major pipelines (notably NOT 'Waha-Nasser') — but I fetched that page directly and this pipeline list does NOT appear anywhere in the actual HTML; the search tool's synthesis appears to have fabricated/merged it from elsewhere, so I am explicitly NOT relying on or citing it. Net: no independent source of any kind could be found that names a 'Waha-Nasser' gas pipeline, the row's own cited source is both dead and generically non-specific (and is reused wholesale across ~10 other rows), and there is a plausible mechanism for how it could be a conflation (two real, separately-operated Sirte Basin fields/nodes stitched into a pipeline name GEM invented for a network diagram). Recommend treating as an unconfirmed/possible-hallucination entity pending a real primary source (Waha Oil Co / NOC technical document, EIA/USGS Sirte Basin infrastructure map, or a news report) rather than accepting the current spec values (177 km / 24 in / 5.66 bcm/y / operating) at face value. Did not add any refs — nothing passed verification.

concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed real and correctly classified. The sheet's own two citations: (1) a Facebook photo link — 200 live but no extractable text, useless as a spec source (not cited); (2) a World Bank/Tractebel Engineering report 'Fuel Availability & Opportunities for Cost Reduction Report' (Libya: Supporting Electricity Sector Reform, 18 Dec 2017) — verified live (200) via WebFetch + manual pdftotext extraction (url_verifier's automated substring screen false-negatived on this PDF per its own documented PDF-extraction caveat; I confirmed the exact phrases manually). This report independently and repeatedly describes a '34" Coastal Pipeline system with a total longitude of ~1,120 km' connecting Libya's West and East gas network areas via Mellitah (West Entry Point) -> Marsa El Brega -> Benghazi (East Entry Point) — matching GEM's recorded endpoints (Mellitah Complex->Benghazi), diameter (34in, exact match) and length (1164km vs source's ~1120km, ~4% high, within normal rounding tolerance). Status=operating and Fuel=Gas are both well-supported by extensive context (flows, injection, consumption figures) even though the literal word 'operating' isn't required per the confidence-tier rules. Owner1='Libyan National Oil Corp' 100% is plausible: the source states NOC 'is in charge of exploration, production, transportation and commercialization of O&G' and that a NOC subsidiary, General Gas Transmission and Distribution Company (GGT&D, est. 2007), specifically 'construct[s] and manage[s]' the gas distribution/transmission network — so GGT&D may be the more precise operator/owner-of-record than the parent NOC, but NOC as ultimate state owner is not wrong. DUPLICATE CONCERN: the same World Bank source explicitly decomposes this 'Coastal Pipeline' into constituent legs that GEM ALSO tracks as separate ProjectIDs on the in-scope roster: the western leg (871km total) splits into a Mellitah->Tripoli->Khoms trench (222km, ~600 mmscf/d nominal) and a Brega->Khoms trench (645km, ~370 mmscf/d) — the latter length matches P1863 'Brega-Khoms Gas Pipeline' (645km) almost exactly; and the eastern leg is Marsa El Brega->Benghazi (246km, ~410 mmscf/d), the same route as P1862 'Brega-Benghazi Gas Pipeline' (though P1862's recorded length of 396km diverges from the source's 246km for that same leg — a separate P1862 issue, out of scope here but worth flagging to whoever re-audits P1862). P1865 'Tripoli-Mellitah' (158km) and P1864 'Khoms-Tripoli' (201km) together (359km) roughly correspond to the source's single 222km Mellitah-Tripoli-Khoms trench, again not a clean 1:1 match but clearly the same physical corridor split differently. Net effect: GEM appears to carry BOTH a system/network-level 'Coastal Pipeline' entity (P0483, cluster/rollup framing, len 1164/cap 604) AND its physical constituent segments as separate full-attribute rows (P1865/P1864/P1863/P1862) — this is the exact 'dual-level granularity' pattern this project's own reconciliation SOP acknowledges (network-grouping rows vs individual segment rows) and it risks double-counting length/capacity if both are summed in aggregate tracker statistics. This is a structural/dedup issue, not a fabrication — recommend NOT silently deleting either level, but flagging for a maintainer decision on which layer carries the aggregate totals.

concerns.researcher_notes: Roster comparison: P6705 shares the exact name 'Wafa-Mellitah Gas Pipeline' and the same origin ('Wafa Gas Field') as P0484, but its length (524.65 km) matches the real-world figure confirmed by 3 independent sources (~525-530km, see spec finding below), while its diameter (16in) matches the OIL/condensate line's diameter, not the 32in gas trunkline that this row (P0484) correctly carries. This is a strong signature of cross-contamination between two records for the same corridor: P0484 has the right diameter (32in, gas) but a corrupted length; P6705 has the right length but the wrong pipeline's diameter attached to the 'Gas Pipeline' name. Not confirmed as a 100% duplicate without seeing P6705's own full sourcing, but the overlap is too specific to be coincidence and warrants a merge/reconciliation pass rather than treating both as independent operating pipelines.

concerns.recommendation: Do not add refs as-is; review for merge/retirement against P1864 (Khoms-Tripoli Gas Pipeline, 201 km) + P1865 (Tripoli-Mellitah Gas Pipeline, 158 km), which already fully cover the Khoms->Mellitah route. concerns.researcher_notes: Both of the wiki page's own citations are dead and neither actually names a standalone 'Khoms-Melita' pipeline. (1) 'Natural Gas Pipelines in Europe, Asia, Africa & Middle East', Harvard worldmap.harvard.edu/data/geonode:natural_gas_pipelines_j96 -> now 404 (verified with url_verifier), and even when live this was a generic global pipeline-map dataset, not a source that names this specific pipeline -- exactly the kind of aggregate citation the task flags as an existence red flag. (2) sirteoil.com.ly/?p=8754 -> the live site has been rebuilt as a JS SPA that serves only a blank shell for this old query-string URL (confirmed 200 but empty content, no article); the Wayback snapshot (archive timestamp 2021-06-19, verified live and containing the expected Arabic terms) recovers the original article, which is a tour report by Sirte Oil Co's board chairman of western-region gas facilities. Crucially, that source does NOT describe a 'Khoms-Melita' pipeline as a discrete object -- it explicitly names the route as two separate lines, quote: "خط 'الخمس - طرابلس' 'طرابلس - مليتة' تم تشغيله مبكراً..." (the 'Khoms-Tripoli' / 'Tripoli-Mellitah' line was commissioned early...), i.e. the exact same segment names GEM already tracks separately as P1864 (Khoms-Tripoli, 201 km) and P1865 (Tripoli-Mellitah, 158 km). The article does use an informal umbrella phrase 'الخط الطولي الخمس مليته' (the Khoms-Mellitah longitudinal line) for job titles/administrative purposes (e.g. 'منسق العمليات والخط الطولي الخمس مليته'), confirming Sirte Oil Co. operates this corridor as a unit -- which supports Operator=Sirte Oil Co as plausible -- but gives no support for a physically distinct 25 km segment called 'Khoms-Melita'. Geographically, Khoms and the Mellitah Complex are roughly 220 km apart by straight line (and ~360 km by the P1864+P1865 route length, consistent with a coastal detour through Tripoli); a 25 km pipeline cannot span that distance, so this cannot be read as a shorthand/simplified version of the same route. I could find zero independent sources (web search in English and Arabic) that describe a distinct 'Khoms-Melita'/'Khoms-Mellitah' pipeline with a 25 km length, 34-inch diameter, or 2 bcm/y capacity -- every hit either is GEM's own wiki page or is unrelated. GEM's own separately-cited Libya Coastal Gas Pipeline page (read for structural context only, not cited here) describes the same Khoms-to-Mellitah stretch as the 'western segment' of that single 1164 km trunk (nominal 600 mmcf/day), reinforcing that this corridor is already modeled elsewhere in the dataset (P0483 in aggregate; P1864+P1865 at segment level) and that P1789's very short 25 km / 2 bcm/y figures do not correspond to any documented physical asset. Net: existence of *a* Khoms-Mellitah gas corridor is real, but the specific object recorded under P1789 (a standalone 25 km, 34in, 2 bcm/y line) looks like a duplicate/fragment -- most plausibly a mis-scoped or badly digitized artifact from the (now-dead) Harvard worldmap dataset -- rather than a distinct physical pipeline. Location field is also internally inconsistent: EndState/Province is populated with 'Melita Port', which is not a real Libyan province (the real province for Mellitah is Nuqat al Khams, as recorded correctly on P0483/P0484), another sign this row was carelessly assembled.

concerns.recommendation: Reconcile with P0483 (Libya Coastal Gas Pipeline, Mellitah Complex->Benghazi, len=1164km) -- check whether P0483's length/capacity totals already include this Brega->Benghazi stretch (and likely also P1863 Brega-Khoms, P1864 Khoms-Tripoli, P1865 Tripoli-Mellitah) as its 'eastern segment', which would double-count length/capacity if both the aggregate P0483 and the individual segment P1862 are summed in tracker-wide totals.

This is a real segment/aggregate double-count risk, not proof of an outright duplicate -- GEM sometimes legitimately tracks both a named backbone/system and its constituent segments as distinct rows, and Libya Herald's use of 'Brega-Benghazi gas pipeline' as a standalone named entity (with its own incident history and named operator, Brega Petroleum Marketing) shows the segment does have its own real-world identity. concerns.recommendation: Reconcile with P0483 (Libya Coastal Gas Pipeline, Mellitah Complex->Benghazi, 1164km) -- confirm P0483's length/capacity are a genuinely separate physical asset and not simply the sum of this segment plus P1862/P1864/P1865, which would double-count length and capacity across the tracker if both the aggregate and its constituent segments are totalled.
concerns.researcher_notes: The same World Bank/Tractebel report frames Libya's coastal gas system as ONE network of two 'legs': an eastern leg (Brega->Benghazi) and a western leg spanning 871km from Mellitah to Marsa El Brega, which it explicitly splits into two named sub-segments -- 'Mellitah to Tripoli and then to Khoms (222 km)' and 'Brega to Khoms (645 km)' -- i.e. this exact GEM row (P1863) is described in the source as ONE HALF of the western leg of the same corridor that GEM separately tracks end-to-end as P0483 (Mellitah Complex->Benghazi, 1164km). Summing GEM's own segment chain -- P1865 Tripoli-Mellitah (158km) + P1864 Khoms-Tripoli (201km) + P1863 Brega-Khoms (645km) + P1862 Brega-Benghazi (396km) = 1400km -- overshoots P0483's 1164km, while the WB report's own component lengths (222km Mellitah-Khoms + 645km Khoms-Brega + 246km Brega-Benghazi = 1113km) land close to P0483's 1164km, suggesting P0483 already represents the corridor as a whole and the individually-named segment rows (including this one) may be double-counted if summed alongside it in tracker-wide length/capacity totals. This is not proof P1863 should be deleted/merged -- GEM legitimately tracks both system-level and segment-level entities elsewhere, and the WB report itself independently names 'El Khoms - El Brega' as a distinct managed segment with its own utilization/bottleneck data (i.e. it has real standalone operational identity, matching GEM's segmentation choice) -- but it is a genuine aggregate/segment overlap risk worth a human reconciliation pass across P0483/P1862/P1863/P1864/P1865, consistent with the same flag raised on the P1862 (Brega-Benghazi) shard.

concerns.recommendation: Cross-check/likely merge with P0599 (Nasser-Brega Oil Pipeline, GOIT) before re-referencing; do not publish the 277km/14.87 bcm/y gas-specific figures without independent support for a distinct gas line.
concerns.researcher_notes: The sheet's only cited source for this row (OPEC Annual Statistics Bulletin 2012, ASB2012.pdf) fails to name the pipeline at all: ran url_verifier against the live PDF for 'Nasser-Brega', 'Brega', and 'pipeline' -- all three came back FAIL ('200 but missing expected'). So the row's existing citation is a generic aggregate document that provides zero specific support -- exactly the existence-flag scenario. Independent web search turned up a SEPARATE, well-documented GEM entry, 'Nasser-Brega Oil Pipeline' (gem.wiki/Nasser-Brega_Oil_Pipeline), which is tracked in GOIT as ProjectID P0599: Fuel=Oil, Status=operating, StartLocation=Nasser oilfield, EndLocation=Brega, StartState/Province=EndState/Province=Al Wahat, Diameter=36in, Length=171.62km, Capacity=38.84 mtpa, Owner=Libyan National Oil Corp 100%, built October 1961 (also known as Zaltan-Al Brayqah), operator Sirte Oil Company. P1866's endpoints (Nasser oilfield -> Mersa Brega/Al Wahat) and diameter (36in) match P0599 EXACTLY; only the length (277km vs 171.62km) and capacity (14.87 bcm/y vs 38.84 mtpa, different units entirely -- gas volume vs oil mass) differ. Independently verified via offshore-technology.com that the Nasser field itself is classified as a conventional OIL field operated by Sirte Oil (not a gas field), and via Wikipedia's Zelten oil field article (Zelten = Nasser field's earlier name) that the field's documented pipeline connection is 'the main line between the Zelten field and Brega' in an oil-production context (associated gas is used for gas-lift, not described as a separate transmission pipeline to Brega). GEM's own GGIT gas-tracker page for this row is also strikingly thin (single-sentence description, single non-supporting citation, StartLocation left blank in the mainsheet, a stray unverifiable Facebook photo link sitting in ResearcherNotes that also does not mention Nasser or Brega when checked). Taken together this reads as a likely mis-tracked/duplicated entry -- the same physical Nasser-to-Brega corridor recorded once (correctly, well-cited) as an oil pipeline in GOIT and a second time (thinly, uncited) as a gas pipeline in GGIT -- rather than genuine evidence of a distinct 36in/277km gas transmission line on this route. Could not fully rule out that Nasser field's associated/lift gas is evacuated via a real parallel gas line, but no independent source names one, so verdict is concern rather than confirmed.

concerns.recommendation: Reclassify PipelineType from 'transmission' to 'gathering'.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's controlled vocab for PipelineType is transmission / gathering / distribution (docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md). nsenergybusiness.com (verified OK) states explicitly this 8.5km/14in DP3-DP4 line's purpose is to 'transport raw gas from DP3 to DP4' — i.e. it moves unprocessed wellstream gas between two adjacent offshore production platforms so it can be treated at DP4, not treated/sales-quality gas moving to market. That is a textbook inter-platform gathering line, not a transmission trunk. (By contrast the downstream P7617 segment DP4-Sabratha carries already-dehydrated gas + condensate toward the onshore complex, which is a more defensible transmission call — that segment is out of scope here but worth a look too.) The sheet's only cited ref for PipelineType (jpt.spe.org) never uses the word 'transmission' or 'gathering' at all — it just describes the project generally — so the current classification isn't actually supported by its own citation.

concerns.recommendation: MOVE TO GOIT - this is the 4in CONDENSATE line, not gas. Unlike P6705 (cluster B) and P6713 (cluster D), GOIT does NOT already carry it: the 2026-07-28 GOIT snapshot has no Bouri or Bahr Assalam row among Libya's 57 oil rows. So this one is a genuine reclassification that creates a new GOIT row, not a delete. Confirm the GOIT check still holds at apply-time. concerns.researcher_notes: [cluster C: Bouri-Bahr Assalam: a real twinned pair (sourced) - but the 4in is condensate] RESOLVED WITH SOURCES - see P1859 for the twinned-pair evidence. The 4in of the pair is the condensate line. This is the THIRD condensate line found sitting in Libya's gas tracker in one batch (P6705, P6713, P6709), which is why the pattern is escalated as a class defect rather than three isolated fixes. Note the dispositions differ and must not be applied uniformly: two are deletes because GOIT already holds the asset, this one is a move because GOIT does not. ROOT CAUSE of the capacity figure: these come from OPEC ASB Table 4.10, whose column header reads '(1,000 scm/yr)'; the ingest took the raw cell and labelled it 'scm/yr', dropping the x1000. THE WORSE, SEPARATE DEFECT: 'scm/y' and 'scm/yr' are not units GGIT's CapacityBcm/y formula converts - all four Libya rows using them (P1858, P6709, P6713, P6714) compute CapacityBcm/y = 0.00 or blank and contribute ZERO to any Libya gas capacity total in the published tracker. Tracker-wide only 8 rows use this unit string: these 4 plus 4 Algeria rows (P6616, P6617, P6618, P6620), and all 8 read zero. Every other scm-family row in GGIT uses MMSCMD, which converts fine.

concerns.recommendation: Reclassify Fuel (and likely move out of the gas-pipeline tracker): the operator's own site states the 16-inch line is the OIL/CONDENSATE pipeline, not gas.
concerns.researcher_notes: P6705 is GEM's 'Pipeline 2' segment of the Wafa-Mellitah system: 16 in diameter, 524.65 km -- this matches exactly the 16-inch leg of the twin-pipeline system. In other words the 32-inch line (= GEM's P0484, 'Pipeline 1', already correctly Fuel=Gas) carries the gas, and the 16-inch line (= this row, P6705, 'Pipeline 2') carries OIL/CONDENSATE, not gas. GEM currently has P6705's Fuel field set to 'Gas' -- that appears to be wrong; it should be an oil/condensate/NGL line, which likely also means it does not belong in a Libya *gas* pipeline tracker at all (or should be flagged as a liquids line associated with the gas project). Diameter (16 in) itself is correctly recorded and independently confirmed. Only one independent primary source explicitly states the commodity split (mellitahog.ly), so tier=medium on this specific classification claim even though existence/routing is high-tier; recommend a human double-check before reclassifying given the consequence (moving the row out of a gas tracker).

concerns.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: real infrastructure, not a hallucination. The Bahr Essalam gas & condensate field (offshore Libya, operated by Mellitah Oil & Gas, the 50/50 NOC-Eni JV) and its onshore link to the Mellitah Complex are independently documented by offshore-technology.com (https://www.offshore-technology.com/projects/bahr-essalam-gas-and-condensate-field/), a professional oil & gas projects database, confirmed live via url_verifier with tokens 'condensate'/'10in' both present. DUPLICATE check: the gem.wiki page 'Bahr Assalam-Mellitah gas pipeline' (fetched directly, since gem.wiki blocks WebFetch's default UA — 403 — but resolves 200 with a browser UA) documents TWO sub-entries on one page: Pipeline '1' (Operator Mellitah O&G, 109 km, 36in, capacity 9,199,943 scm/yr, Start 2005) = GEM ProjectID P1855, and Pipeline '2' (109 km, 10in, capacity 465,166 scm/yr, Start 2018) = this row, P6713. These are NOT duplicates of each other: different diameters, different in-service years, and offshore-technology.com independently corroborates a multi-line system ('production pipelines, piggy-backed service lines...') plus confirms Phase I first gas in 2005 (matches P1855's 2005) and Phase II first gas July 2018 (matches P6713's 2018) via FID-2015/first-gas-2018 language. So the split into two ProjectIDs for two physically distinct, differently-timed lines is legitimate — recommend AGAINST merging.

CLASSIFICATION CONCERN (the real finding): offshore-technology.com's own project writeup distinguishes THREE separate lines from this field: (1) a 32in, 540km SEA LINE to the Green Stream compression station carrying export sales gas to Italy (a different pipeline, not this row); (2) a 36in line from the Sabratha platform to the onshore Mellitah plant carrying GAS — this matches P1855/Pipeline '1'; and (3), verbatim: 'Condensate is directly pumped and conveyed through a 10in diameter pipeline to Mellitah for further treatment and export.' That 10-inch condensate line is an exact diameter match for THIS row (P6713/Pipeline '2', Diameter=10in, currently ref'd to ASB2017 and confirmed live). GEM's mainsheet nonetheless records Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission for P6713. The independent source is unambiguous that the 10in line's cargo is condensate (a liquid), not gas. I could not find a second independent source explicitly re-describing this exact 10in segment (OPEC ASB PDFs are generic OPEC-country aggregate statistical bulletins — confirmed by pulling ASB2013.pdf and grepping it: no pipeline-level table, only national production/reserves tables — they do not actually discuss this specific pipeline's cargo type), so tier=medium (one strong, on-point independent source) rather than high. Flagging as concern rather than silently passing per the instructions on material disagreement.

ATTRIBUTION: Owner (Libyan National Oil Corp 50% / Eni SpA 50%) is consistent with the well-established Mellitah Oil & Gas B.V. JV structure and the existing mellitahog.ly ref (live, 200) — no issue found. Location (Bahr Assalam/Sabratha field → Mellitah Complex, Libya) is consistent with offshore-technology.com. Start Year 2018 is corroborated: offshore-technology.com states Phase II FID completed 2015 and 'Phase two achieved first gas in July 2018' — solid match for this row's StartYear1=2018.

So the real nameplate capacity is roughly 774-1,064 MMcf/d, not 20 MMcf/d — a ~40-50x discrepancy, almost certainly a unit-conversion or data-entry error (e.g. a bcm figure mis-mapped into an MMcf/d field, or a decimal/order-of-magnitude slip). This is corroborated by 3 independent sources (Reuters, Wikipedia, RT-Arabic) all agreeing with each other and all disagreeing with GEM, so flagging per the 'material disagreement' rule rather than silently passing it. concerns.researcher_notes: The Zueitina source states the project's gas delivery targets in mmcf/day, not bcm/y: Phase 1 = ~250 million standard cubic feet/day; full build-out (all phases) = ~1500 million standard cubic feet/day. Converting for cross-check: 1500 mmcf/d x 28,316.85 m3/mmcf = ~42.475 million m3/day (Mm3/d) -- this is suspiciously exactly GEM's recorded Capacity figure of 42.48. That strongly suggests GEM's Capacity value was taken directly from this project's daily mmcf/d target, correctly converted to million m3/DAY, but then mislabeled with CapacityUnits='bcm/y' (billion m3/YEAR) instead of the correct daily unit. Annualizing correctly: 42.475 Mm3/d x 365 = ~15.5 bcm/y -- so even at the FULL eventual build-out target, capacity should read ~15.5 bcm/y, not 42.48 bcm/y (a ~2.7x overstatement as currently recorded); and Phase 1 alone (250 mmcf/d) is only ~2.6 bcm/y. concerns.researcher_notes: Evidence supports a genuine double-count risk, though it does not resolve cleanly to 'yes, definitely redundant' vs 'no.' (1) P1862 Brega-Benghazi (396km) + P1863 Brega-Khoms (645km) + P1864 Khoms-Tripoli (201km) + this row P1865 Tripoli-Mellitah (158km) sum to exactly 1,400 km, retracing the identical Mellitah<->Benghazi coastal corridor that P0483 'Libya Coastal Gas Pipeline' also covers end-to-end as a single aggregate row (1,164 km). Both the 4-segment set and P0483 trace back to overlapping citations: the recovered OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (which lists ONLY the 4 discrete Sirte-Oil-operated segments -- Brega/Benghazi, Brega/Khoms, Khoms/Tripoli, Tripoli/Mellitah -- with no aggregate 'Coastal Pipeline' total line of its own) and the World Bank/Tractebel 2017-18 report (which P0483's shard also used, and which this shard used independently). (2) The two source families do NOT even agree on how many physical trenches make up the western half: OPEC's table (and hence GEM's P1864/P1865 split) treats Khoms-Tripoli and Tripoli-Mellitah as two separate accounting segments (359 km combined), while the World Bank/Tractebel engineering report models the identical Mellitah<->Khoms run as ONE trench of only 222 km -- a 137 km (62%) gap that cannot be explained by rounding or unit error. This suggests OPEC's per-segment table may reflect tariff/ownership accounting boundaries (each stretch separately reported by Sirte Oil) rather than necessarily four separately-built physical pipelines, and raises the possibility the Tripoli split point is not a real physical joint recognized in independent engineering literature. (3) Separately, at least one LATER, smaller-spec 'Melitah-Tripoli'/'Tripoli-Mellitah' pipeline was built/completed circa 2005-2006 (ognnews.com project report; Al Wasat News 2006, Punj Lloyd contract, ~120 km, 200 MMcf/d, built to supply Zawiya power station) -- a different physical asset from the OPEC-table line this row's exact values (158km/34in/16.99 bcm/y) match, adding a further identification wrinkle but not itself evidence of double-counting against P0483. Net read: strong circumstantial evidence that P0483 (aggregate) and the P1862-P1865 segment set describe the SAME underlying physical corridor from overlapping sourcing, with an unreconciled ~20% total-length gap (1,400 km segment-sum vs 1,164 km aggregate) and an internally inconsistent western-half segmentation (OPEC's 2-segment Khoms-Tripoli/Tripoli-Mellitah split vs World Bank/Tractebel's single Mellitah-Khoms trench). This is a candidate for human review to decide whether P0483 should be retired/merged now that the more granular segment rows exist, or whether the segment set should itself be re-consolidated (e.g. merging P1864+P1865 into one Khoms-Mellitah row) to match the independent engineering source's trench boundaries -- not something this researcher can resolve unilaterally without fabricating a reconciliation.

concerns.researcher_notes: Read as: (b)-leaning but with an important caveat, not a clean (a) or (b). Evidence suggests P1866 (gas) and P0599 (oil) are most likely genuinely SEPARATE physical pipelines sharing the same Nasser(Zelten)-Brega corridor and nominal diameter, rather than one line double-entered across trackers — but GEM's own length value for the gas line (277 km) is unsupported and looks like an error, which is a separate problem from the redundancy question. Evidence for two distinct lines: (1) OPEC ASB 2012 lists them as two separate table rows in two separate tables — 'Nasser/Al-Brayqah' (Sirte, 172, 36, capacity 292 [implicitly Mt/kt-scale, oil units]) in Table 4.9 'Crude oil pipelines' (p.71), and 'Nasser/Brega' (Sirte Oil, 172, 36, capacity 14,868,309 [1,000 scm/yr]) in Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines' (p.75) — same owner/operator (Sirte Oil), same length (172) and diameter (36in), but a completely different, gas-appropriate capacity unit, i.e. OPEC itself treats them as two accounted flows, not a copy-paste of one row. (2) An independent 1970s-commissioning engineering incident-report paper (title: 'Explosion in the Gas Pipeline 36-inch diameter, Zelten-Brega', Hussein Albashik) describes a distinct '36in gas pipeline from Zelten to Brega' with its own rupture history (Aug 2014, Km 18) and 150 mmscfd design capacity from its 1970 commissioning — i.e. a real, physically documented gas asset independent of the 1961-built crude oil line (whose GEM wiki summary independently gives commissioning October 1961, separate from this line's 1970 commissioning) (this source itself is uncitable — academia.edu returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and url_verifier — so treat this only as directional evidence, not a stageable ref). (3) A WebSearch synthesis (source unconfirmed) also describes 'a 30-inch gas pipeline' linking Zelten field to the Brega LNG/petrochemical complex, suggesting there may even be more than one gas-carrying line/lateral in this corridor, further supporting that the gas and oil assets are not simply the same line re-entered. Caveat / what is NOT resolved: I found no source giving 277 km for the gas line specifically — every source on this corridor (OPEC, Wikipedia Zelten field, the WebSearch-synthesized 170km figure) converges on ~169-172 km, i.e. essentially the SAME length as the oil pipeline P0599 (171.62 km). If the two lines are truly parallel and co-built/co-routed (which fits '36in, Sirte Oil, same corridor' appearing twice in OPEC's own 2012 tables), a shared/near-identical length would be expected and is not itself evidence of duplication — but it does mean GEM's currently entered 277 km for P1866 cannot be independently justified as reflecting a materially longer or different route than P0599's 171.62 km, and the discrepancy should be resolved (most likely by correcting P1866's length toward ~172 km) independently of the redundancy question. Net read: keep both P0599 (oil) and P1866 (gas) as distinct entities — the weight of evidence favors two real, separate, same-corridor pipelines — but recommend a length correction on P1866, not a merge/removal of either row.

concerns.researcher_notes: OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (p.75, Libya) lists the Sirte Oil Company gathering network as SIX distinct milepost-to-milepost segments, each with its own length/diameter/capacity, not one aggregated line: Attahaddy/km-91.5 (25mi, 30in, 28,320,589); Km-81.5/Brega [= P1868] (82mi, 30in, 8,496,177); Raguba/km-110 (88mi, 20in, 3,964,882); Intesar/Sahel (80mi, 30in, 19,824,412); Sahel/km-81.5 (49mi, 30in, 19,541,206); Km-91.5/Brega (92mi, 36in, 21,240,442) — all attributed to 'Sirte Oil' as owner/operator, all reported in units of 1,000 scm/yr capacity. No source found (OPEC or otherwise) that describes this network as a single pipeline/line rather than a chain of discrete named segments. The official statistical source itself treats Km-81.5/Brega as a standalone segment with unique specs distinct from the other five (different length, and Sahel/km-81.5 and Km-91.5/Brega in particular have different endpoints and different capacity/diameter than Km-81.5/Brega despite sharing the 'km-81.5' or 'Brega' token), which supports these being genuine separate segments of one connected gathering trunk rather than double-counted duplicates of the same physical pipe. No evidence found either way of GEM having mis-split a single segment into two rows; based on available sources, no redundancy is indicated for P1868 specifically.

GEM's separate P1867 'Attahaddy-km-91.5' and P1871 'Sahel-km-81.5' rows correspond to the respective upstream feeder segments in the same OPEC table, reinforcing that the '91.5' and '81.5' junctions are two distinct nodes on the network, each with its own feeder + Brega-bound trunk, not a single shared trunk. No evidence found that P1872 and P1868 should be merged or that either is a phantom duplicate of the other.

concerns.researcher_notes: P3987 (Intisar-Sarir) and P3988 (Fargh-Sarir) read as TWO DISTINCT physical lines, not a double-count, though both feed the same Sarir hub and their names/histories are easy to conflate. Evidence they are separate assets: (1) different named source fields -- Intisar (Sirte Basin concession-103 field) vs. Fargh/Faregh (a different, separately-named Waha field) -- feeding the same downstream Sarir station; (2) different specs in independent, dated source documents -- sirtggp.com's 2020 contract page gives Intisar-Sarir as 20-inch / 114 km, while Waha Oil's own 2020-11-23 news post (cited in the P3988 shard) gives Fargh-Sarir as 97 km, explicitly calling it 'khat al-Fargh-Sarir' (the Fargh-Sarir line) as its own named project, separate from the Intisar line; (3) GEM's own recorded lengths for the two rows (235 km vs 97 km) are far enough apart, and the two independently-sourced values I found (114 km for Intisar-Sarir vs. 97 km for Fargh-Sarir) are also clearly distinct, that this isn't the same segment measured two ways. I did not find a single source describing 'Intisar-Sarir' and 'Fargh-Sarir' as alternate names for one project; every source treats them as separate lines within the same Sirte-Basin-to-Sarir gas-gathering scheme (also distinct from P1861 Farigh-Intesar/Waha-Faregh's OPEC-sourced 110 mi / 177 km line, which runs the other direction, Faregh TO Intesar, not to Sarir). Net read: not a redundancy, but part of a genuinely multi-line network around Intisar/Fargh/Sarir that is easy to mis-merge -- worth a note in country docs that these are parallel/sequential feeder lines, not duplicate records of one pipeline. Also unrelated: a brand-new (April 2026) 42-inch, 130 km 'Intisar A/103-Brega' pipeline just entered trial operation per NOC/Libya Observer/Pipeline Technology Journal reporting -- confirmed via WebFetch this is a DIFFERENT route (different diameter, length, and destination -- Brega, not Sarir) and not a duplicate or update candidate for P3987/P3988; flagging only so it isn't mistaken for this pipeline in later research.

concerns.researcher_notes: P3988 (Fargh–Sarir, this row) and P1861 (Farigh-Intesar, per this batch's own P1861 shard) are NOT duplicates of each other: P1861 traces to OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 data from 2011 (110 mi / 177 km, 24 in diameter, 7.08 bcm/y capacity -- an older, pre-existing Waha line running Fargh field to the Intisar field/103 complex), while P3988 traces to a 2020 Waha Oil Company announcement of a NEWLY commissioned 97 km line running Fargh field to Sarir GAS/POWER STATION -- different destination, different specs, different vintage, and my primary Waha-2020 source itself distinguishes the two: it describes the Fargh-Sarir line (this row) separately from ongoing supply 'to the Intisar A field ... 70 million cubic meters of gas' (the P1861 corridor), i.e. Fargh field feeds two distinct downstream lines. Good evidence these are two real, separate pieces of infrastructure. P3987 (Intisar–Sarir) is a different question: per GEM's own wiki text, P3987 is described as running from Intisar oil field (Sirte Basin) to Sarir oil field (Cyrenaica), status is explicitly '(presumed operating)' based solely on a 2017 agreement with 'no direct evidence' (GEM's own wording), sourced to a single eanlibya.com URL I could not locate/verify (search engines returned no matching eanlibya.com page under that slug) plus a generic Waha Facebook page and a wahaoil.ly article titled 'إستئناف تغذية خط محطة السرير بشكل اعتيادي' ('resumption of normal supply to the Sarir station LINE') -- that title describes a SUPPLY LINE TO SARIR STATION resuming normal operation, which is the same phrasing/subject as the Fargh–Sarir gas-to-power-station story I independently corroborated for P3988 (Libya Observer 2022-07-24: 'Fargh field ... restarted pumping gas to the Sarir power station'; multiple Arabic sources found this session state plainly 'حقل الفارغ يمثل المصدر الرئيس لتغذية محطة السرير' -- 'the Fargh field is THE MAIN source supplying Sarir station'). I found no independent corroboration anywhere (English or Arabic press, 2017-2026) of a physically distinct 'Intisar oil field to Sarir oil field' gas pipeline separate from the Fargh-to-Sarir line. My working suspicion (not confirmed) is that P3987 may be describing the same underlying Fargh→Sarir gas supply chain/network under an older, less-precise 2017-vintage name (with Intisar possibly an intermediate junction or a source-confusion with the separate Fargh-Intisar line, P1861) rather than a third, independently-built pipeline -- but I could not verify this either way from primary sources, so flagging as UNRESOLVED per protocol rather than asserting duplication. Recommend a human reviewer compare P3987's actual GEM sourcing (the eanlibya.com/wahaoil.ly citations) against this shard's Fargh-Sarir sourcing before any merge/delete decision.

concerns.researcher_notes: STRONG, CORROBORATED FINDING: P6705 (16in) is misclassified -- the 16in Wafa-Mellitah line is the OIL/CONDENSATE line, not a gas line, and does not belong in the gas tracker. Every source found that distinguishes the two parallel Wafa-Mellitah lines by diameter+service agrees, with no exceptions: (1) Offshore Technology's 'Wafa-Mellitah Gas' market-data page: 32in max diameter, carries natural gas / 'on-specification gas', ~13 MMSm3/day. (2) Offshore Technology's separate 'Wafa-Mellitah Oil' market-data page: 16in max diameter, product type 'Crude oil' (condensate). (3) Mellitah Oil & Gas Company Achievements page (operator's own site): 'The 525 Km onshore pipeline system comprises of 32" gas and 16" oil/condensates pipelines. Both pipelines run in parallel from Wafa Desert Plant to Mellitah... the sale gas is exported to Italy and the oil/condensate, after further treatment for LPG fractionation, is exported.' (4) Mellitah Oil & Gas gas-division production page: '32 inches... Carries: On-specification sales gas... ~13 MMSm3/day' vs '16 inches... Carries: Oil and condensate mixture... ~23,000 bbl/d NGL and ~38,000 bbl/d oil/condensate.' (5) Mellitah Oil & Gas Wafa-field site page: the field has a separate 'Gas compression station to Mellitah' and 'Oil pumping station to Mellitah' -- two distinct facilities/lines at the source. (6) Mellitah Oil & Gas Mellitah-Complex page: the Wafa Coastal Plant (within Mellitah Complex) specifically processes 'oil and natural gas liquids from the Wafa field', separately from the Mellitah Plant which handles gas/condensate from the offshore Sabratha platform (Bahr Essalam field) -- i.e. the Wafa-sourced onshore stream landing via the 16in line is treated as an oil/NGL stream, not sales gas. No source anywhere describes a 16in GAS line on this corridor, or a 32in oil/condensate line. CONCLUSION: P6705 (16in, currently in GGIT/gas tracker as 'Wafa-Mellitah Gas Pipeline') and P0484 (32in) are NOT duplicate/redundant entries of the same pipeline -- they are two real, physically distinct, genuinely parallel pipelines, correctly kept as separate rows. But P6705 is in the WRONG TRACKER: by diameter and service it is the oil/condensate line and belongs in GOIT (oil tracker), not GGIT. ACTION FLAG: gem.wiki already has a page titled 'Wafa-Mellitah_Oil_Pipeline' (surfaced incidentally in web search results during this research), which suggests GEM/GOIT may already carry this pipeline as a separate oil-tracker entry under that name -- before reclassifying/moving P6705, check GOIT for an existing 'Wafa-Mellitah Oil Pipeline' row to avoid creating a duplicate; if one already exists, P6705's gas-tracker row is likely a redundant/erroneous entry that should be removed (or corrected in place) rather than moved.

concerns.researcher_notes: NOT a duplicate — sources indicate GEM's P6709 and P1859 represent two genuinely different, parallel physical pipelines on the same Bouri-to-Bahr Essalam/Sabratah corridor, not a double-count of one line. Evidence: OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin tabulates this field-pair as TWO adjacent-but-separate rows in every edition checked (ASB2012, ASB2013, ASB2017): a 10-inch line carrying dehydrated GAS and a 4-inch line carrying CONDENSATE. ASB2017 Table 9.9 makes the pairing explicit: 'Bouri offshore/Bahr Es Salam (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas | 2 x 12 [mi] | 4, 10 [in]' — the '(2)' notation plus '2 x 12' means two parallel 12-mile lines, one 4in and one 10in. Independently, Mellitah Oil & Gas's own 2019 prequalification tender for the 'Bouri Gas Upgrading Project' (BGUP) describes new '10" CS and 4" CS pipelines 20 km long connecting DP4 to Sabratah Platform for dehydrated gas and condensate export' — the same twin-diameter, same-route configuration (gas line + separate condensate line). So P6709 (4in) = the condensate line, P1859 (10in) = the gas line of the same corridor: different specs because they are different pipes, not a GEM data error in that specific sense. Two open caveats worth flagging to the researcher, though: (1) P1859's GEM length (32 km) doesn't match the ~12-12.4 mi (~19-20 km) that ASB2013/ASB2017 converge on for BOTH lines — 32km (=20mi) traces to the earlier ASB2012 edition's figure for that same row, which later ASB editions revised down; P1859's length may merit a separate correction check. (2) The mellitahog.ly 2019 document frames its 10in/4in pipes as NEW/planned BGUP construction (feasibility stage 2019; Saipem's ~$1bn contract 2023; first gas still targeted Sept 2026 per Libya Herald), while the OPEC ASB entries (2011-2013 data) already show a same-diameter pairing years earlier — implying an older, smaller Bouri-Sabratha tie-in predates BGUP and BGUP is now building new/expanded twin lines of the same diameters on the same route. Current-day operating status of GEM's specific P6709/P1859 assets vs. the incoming BGUP lines is not resolved by the sources found; recommend a follow-up check once BGUP reaches first gas (targeted Sept 2026) to confirm whether these rows should be updated to as-built BGUP specs or retired/merged.

concerns.researcher_notes: P6713 and P1855 are NOT simple duplicates of each other, but P6713 IS a genuine misclassification. Multiple independent sources agree the Bahr Essalam (Sabratha platform) field is tied to Mellitah by exactly TWO separate subsea lines, not one: a 36-in line carrying GAS and a 10-in line carrying CONDENSATE (liquids). Offshore Technology: '10-in diameter pipeline through which condensate is directly pumped and conveyed to Mellitah'; Offshore Magazine: '36-in. and 10-in. pipelines taking gas and condensate from the platform 100-km south to Mellitah.' P6713 has diameter=10in — it IS the condensate line, not a second gas line, despite carrying the same 'Gas Pipeline' name as P1855 (diameter=36in, the true gas line). The likely mechanical origin of the GEM duplication: OPEC's own ASB tables list BOTH diameters under one shared row/label ('Bahr Assalam/Mellitah ... 68.2 mi ... 36 in ... 9,199,943' and a second row 'Bahr Assalam/Mellitah ... 68.2 mi ... 10 in ... 465,166', both under the 'Gas pipelines' table heading even though the 10-in line is physically condensate) — someone appears to have carried both OPEC rows into GGIT as two separate 'Gas Pipeline' entities instead of recognizing the second as condensate. Critically, GEM ALREADY tracks this exact 10-in condensate line correctly, under GOIT (oil/NGL tracker): P6457 'Sabratha-Mellitah Condensate Pipeline' — Start='Sabratha platform', End='Mellitah', Length=107 km, Diameter=10 in, Status=operating — near-identical specs to P6713 (Bahr Assalam/Mellitah, 109 km, 10 in, operating). FINDING: P6713 in GGIT (gas) is a duplicate/misclassified twin of P6457 in GOIT (oil/NGL); it belongs in the oil tracker, not the gas tracker, and once reclassified is redundant with the already-existing P6457. Recommend retiring/removing P6713 from GGIT (or merging its provenance into P6457) rather than treating it as a distinct gas pipeline needing its own refs going forward.

concerns.researcher_notes: NOT a double-count — evidence points to two real, parallel gas pipelines, not one line entered twice. Internal comparison: P1858 (34in, capacity 4,134,806) and P6714 (10in, capacity 258,425) share the identical length (131.96 km) and identical start/end (Bu-Attifel Oil Field -> Intesar Oil field, Sirte Basin). OPEC ASB2013 Table 4.10 ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2012', p.~74-75, recovered via Wayback, pdftotext-confirmed) lists them as TWO SEPARATE table rows with different operators: 'Bu-Attifel/Intesar   Mellitah Oil and Gas   82.46mi   34in   4,134,806' and 'Bu-Attifel/Intesar (103A)   Eni Oil   82.46mi   10in   258,425' -- exact match to P1858 and P6714 respectively, down to the capacity figures. OPEC ASB2017 Table 9.9 (2016 data, recovered via Wayback) independently corroborates this across a later edition, listing the connection as 'Bu Attifel/Intisar (2)' -- explicitly '(2)' = two lines -- '2 x 82mi', diameters '34, 10', joint owner field 'Mellitah Oil & Gas, Eni Oil' (i.e. one line per operator). Two OPEC editions four years apart, independently compiled, agree that this is a twinned/parallel pipeline pair (same corridor, different operators/diameters/capacities), not a single pipeline double-entered. Recommend: NOT a candidate for merging/removal; if anything, GEM's Owner/Operator data for these two rows should be checked to confirm P1858=Mellitah Oil & Gas and P6714=Eni Oil, matching the OPEC operator split (out of scope for this ref-only shard).

Both sources describe this as the combined/shared corridor length for BOTH parallel lines, not a length unique to a 16in gas service.

Mellitah Oil & Gas's own Wafa Field site page confirms the field (NC169A concession, ~540 km SW of Tripoli, ~160 km south of Ghadames, on the Libya-Algeria border) has a 'Gas compression station to Mellitah' and a separate 'Oil pumping station to Mellitah' -- i.e. two distinct pipeline take-off points at Wafa field itself, one per commodity. Treated as a minor inconsistency on Offshore Technology's auto-generated market-data page, not a contradiction of GEM's EndLocation.

GEM records Owner1='BASF' 100% with no ref. Both OPEC ASB editions (2012 Table 4.10, 2017 Table 9.9) name the pipeline's owner/operator column simply 'Wintershall', never 'BASF'. An independent 2015 pumpsandsystems.com trade article states plainly that 'Wintershall' is 'a BASF subsidiary' operating the Jakhira gas processing plant -- this is the source that most directly supports the GEM value as a defensible parent-company simplification (Wintershall Aktiengesellschaft/Wintershall Holding GmbH was a wholly BASF-owned entity before the 2019 DEA merger created the jointly-owned Wintershall Dea). VALUE-CONTRADICTION FLAG (do not silently overwrite -- flag only): (1) USGS Minerals Yearbook 2016 (Table 2, Libya) lists the Jakhira/As-Sarah/Nakhla/Tauma concession itself as a 'Wintershall joint venture [National Oil Corp. (NOC), 51%, and Wintershall Holding GmbH, 49%]' -- i.e. at the concession/equity level Wintershall Holding GmbH held only a 49% interest, not 100%, so 'BASF 100%' is at best a simplification collapsing two different corporate layers (BASF's ownership of the Wintershall entity vs. Wintershall's minority equity share of the actual Libyan concession JV). (2) Wintershall Dea's own newsroom (verified, independent of OPEC) confirms operatorship of these exact Sirte Basin fields (Jakhira/As-Sarah, Area 91) was transferred on 29 October 2020 from WIAG to Sarir Oil Operations (SOO), a new joint venture between WIAG and Libya's NOC -- meaning even 'Wintershall' alone is now a stale operator/owner attribution; SOO (the WIAG/NOC JV) is the more current entity. Recommend flagging Owner1='BASF' as an Update-candidate correction (Wintershall / Sarir Oil Operations JV), not applying it here -- staging only, per protocol.

A U.S. Department of the Treasury press release (tg1114, sanctions-related) independently lists Sirte Oil Co. among the companies owned/controlled by Libya's state-owned National Oil Corporation, establishing the chain Sirte Oil -> wholly-owned NOC operating subsidiary. This supports GEM's Owner1 = 'Libyan National Oil Corp' (100%) as a parent-company rollup of the OPEC-named direct operator, rather than either source literally naming 'Libyan National Oil Corp' as the pipeline's owner. Tier held at medium (not high) because both citable sources confirm the *relationship* rather than either directly stating NOC as owner-of-record for this specific pipeline; Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article says the same but was not cited as a third source to avoid tertiary-only reliance.

OPEC ASB Table 4.10 lists 'Owner or operator' = 'Zueitina' for this line. The project page is itself hosted on زueitina.com.ly and describes the project as one Zueitina was entrusted with by NOC ('عهدت المؤسسة الوطنية للنفط لشركة الزويتينة للنفط للمتابعة والإشراف عليه' — 'NOC entrusted Zueitina Oil Co. with following up and supervising it'), i.e. self-attributed operatorship. OperatorLocalLanguage 'شركة الزويتينة للنفط' matches the company's own Arabic name as it appears verbatim on its site.

Zueitina's own 'About Us' history page (Arabic version, Wayback 2011, and the current English version, Wayback 2026 — same content, 15 years apart) states verbatim: for its 'Muqasama' (production-sharing) fields, ownership is '81% المؤسسة الوطنية للنفط [NOC] — 14.25% أوكسيدنتال [Occidental] — 4.75% أو.ام.في [OMV]' — an EXACT match to the brief's Owner1/2/3 values and percentages. Both language mirrors are the same company/source, so independence is false (1 source, corroborated across two snapshots in time rather than across two organizations). CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: the SAME about-us page lists field '103أ' (Intisar/103A — i.e. the very field this pipeline originates from) under the heading 'حقول الانتصار (المشاركة) النفطية' — the 'Musharaka' (participation) field category — whose ownership split is stated elsewhere on the same page as 51% NOC / 36.75% Occidental / 12.25% OMV, NOT the 81/14.25/4.75 'Muqasama' split the brief lists. So while 81/14.25/4.75 is a real, exact, sourced Zueitina ownership split, it may be the wrong category for this specific field/pipeline — the correct split per the same source could instead be 51/36.75/12.25. Flagging for review rather than silently 'fixing' the mainsheet; tier kept at medium given the source is strong but the category match is in question.

World Bank/Tractebel report: 'NOC, established in 1970, is the main company...in charge of exploration, production, transportation and commercialization of O&G'; notes the 2007 creation of General Gas Transmission & Distribution Co (GGT&D) as an NOC downstream-gas subsidiary. LibyaReview (1 May 2023, independent) directly states the Brega-Khoms segment of this system is 'operated by the state-owned National Oil Corporation (NOC) through its subsidiary, the Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company.' OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (Wayback-recovered) lists 'Sirte Oil' as owner/operator of the Brega/Benghazi, Brega/Khoms, Khoms/Tripoli and Tripoli/Mellitah segments. All three sources triangulate on the same fact set: state-owned NOC is the parent owner, operating this pipeline through its wholly state-owned subsidiary Sirte Oil -- consistent with the sheet's Owner1='Libyan National Oil Corp', 100%.

Neither source names the Defa-Brega line individually or gives an exact ownership percentage, so this supports the general claim (NOC/state ownership of Libya's onshore gas transport network, encompassing Waha- and Sirte Oil-operated infrastructure) rather than a line-item-specific 100% figure; no contradicting ownership claim was found for this line.

wahaoil.ly's own 2021-01-04 post (Wayback) describes Waha Oil Company's own engineering/operations teams at Al-Fareg field restoring gas supply/compression into this exact Intisar(A)-Sarir line -- a specific, direct match. new_rows.name: Farigh-Brega Gas Pipeline

values.OtherEnglishNames: Al-Intisar to Brega Gas Pipeline; Zueitina Field 103-Sirte Oil Line 36B Gas Pipeline
values.EndLocation: Mersa Brega (via Km 91 complex / Sirte Oil Line 36B)
values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: Endpoints known from press reporting (Zueitina Oil Company's Field 103/103A supply base, fed by the Farigh/Al-Faragh field in the Sirte Basin, running ~130km to a tie-in with Sirte Oil Company's existing 42in Line 36B at the Km 91 complex, which feeds the Brega coastal/gas-distribution network) but no official GIS geometry located for this specific 2006-2026 build. Point-A-to-point-B only — RouteAccuracy='low'.
values.Background: Originally contracted in 2006: Zueitina Oil Company (ZOC, a National Oil Corp subsidiary) issued a letter of intent to China Petroleum Engineering & Construction Corp (CPECC) for a 42in pipeline (215km as originally scoped) from ZOC's Field 103A supply base to the Brega coastal network, carrying gas from the Faregh/Al-Faragh field and ZOC's own concession (contract value ~LD41.3m/$30m). Construction was halted amid the pre-2011 unrest/civil conflict and the line sat unfinished for roughly 16 years. NOC revived the project, commissioning a first ~30km phase in March 2026 (gas flowing from the Farigh field into the existing 42in Sirte trunkline at Km 91, reaching Brega by month's end), then completing and beginning a full-line trial run of the 42in, 130km pipeline in April 2026 (NOC Chairman Masoud Suleiman publicly hailed the completion), recovering roughly 150 MMcf/d of previously flared gas for domestic supply and export.

new_rows.researcher_notes:
MATCH CHECK (done first, per rule 4): re-verified against P1856 Intesar-Brega Gas Pipeline (333km, 42in, Intesar Oil field → Mersa Brega, operating, Owner=Waha JV [NOC 59.18%/ConocoPhillips 16.33%/TotalEnergies 16.33%/Hess 8.16%]) and against every other Libya gas row (38 existing, incl. P1861 Farigh-Intesar 177km/24in and P3988 Fargh-Sarir 97km, both also Waha-JV-owned lines that happen to share the 'Farigh' field name). None match this candidate's specific route/history: P1856's start point is the deep-Sirte-Basin 'Intesar Oil field' (a distinct, well-established GEM entity used across P1873/P1858/P3987/P1861), 333km from Brega — more than 2.5x this candidate's built length, already operating, and owned by the Waha IOC joint venture, not by Zueitina Oil Company. This candidate is a separate, coastal-proximity 42in line (130km) from Zueitina Oil Company's own Field 103/103A (fed by the Farigh/Al-Faragh field) tying into the existing Line 36B trunk at Km91 — confirmed distinct by the original 2006 MEED contract history (CPECC awarded a Zueitina-Oil-Company pipeline, gas from 'the Faregh field and ZOC's own concession', explicitly not a Waha/Intesar project) and by the 2026 completion reporting (NOC chairman ties it to 'Zueitina Field 103' specifically). => new_row, not a duplicate or a needed correction to P1856.

ADD-THRESHOLD (all three met, and exceeded — this is past FID, it's built and in trial operation): (a) sponsor = National Oil Corp via Zueitina Oil Company / Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Co, original EPC contractor CPECC (2006); (b) endpoints = Libya, Zueitina Field 103/Farigh field supply base → Km91 tie-in to Sirte Oil's Line 36B / Brega network; (c) concrete step = first 30km phase commissioned March 2026, full 42in/130km line completed and in trial operation April 2026 (NOC Chairman Suleiman publicly announced completion).

SOURCE INDEPENDENCE: 13 URLs verified live via url_verifier (12/13 passed the content screen; the 13th, libyaobserver's in-brief, is a 200 real page that simply doesn't restate the '130' figure — a content false-negative, not a dead link, kept only as trial-operation-status corroboration, not for the length value). Corroborating chains are structurally independent: Pipeline Journal, Ecofinagency, Libya Observer, North Africa Post, Libya Herald, PGJ (Pipeline & Gas Journal), Steelradar, MEED (2026 + a separate contemporaneous 2006 MEED piece on the original CPECC contract), and Gurutrade — nine distinct outlets across March and April 2026, none a reprint of another (each carries independent phrasing/detail), comfortably clearing the >=2 independent-source bar.

STATUS: set to 'construction' rather than 'operating'. Libya Herald's language ('now transports gas... reducing flaring while supplying domestic consumers and export markets') reads as active operation, but the majority of April 2026 sources (PGJ, Ecofinagency, Pipeline Journal, MEED, Gurutrade) frame the April milestone explicitly as a 'trial run'/'testing'/'experimental operation' stage, not a declared commercial in-service date — conservatively kept at construction pending a clearer 'commissioned'/'in commercial operation' statement in a future update. StartYear1 intentionally left blank per the Status=construction ⇒ no StartYear1 convention.

OWNER/FIELD-IDENTITY CAVET (flag for future researcher): sourcing on exactly which field/company underlies this pipeline is not fully consistent across outlets. Libya Herald and the original 2006 MEED piece are explicit and specific: Zueitina Oil Company's Field 103/103A, fed by the Farigh/Al-Faragh field, both wholly NOC lineage (no IOC JV) — this is what's staged as Owner ('Libyan National Oil Corp [100.%]' / Parent 'National Oil Corp [100.00%]', matching the convention used on other 100%-NOC Libya gas rows e.g. P1862/P1863/P1868). However, Pipeline Journal's March piece instead names 'Waha Oil Company' plus IOC partners TotalEnergies and ConocoPhillips as operating the 'Farigh field' feeding this line — the same JV that owns the unrelated P1861 Farigh-Intesar and P3988 Fargh-Sarir pipelines, which also draw on a field called 'Farigh'. This looks like a single outlet conflating two different Libyan 'Farigh' fields (Zueitina's coastal Field 103 vs Waha's inland Sirte Basin field of the same name) rather than evidence this is a Waha-JV asset — no other outlet (incl. the contemporaneous, detailed Libya Herald piece with a direct NOC Chairman quote, and the 2006 MEED contract history) mentions Waha/TotalEnergies/ConocoPhillips in connection with this specific 130km/Km91/Line 36B project. Staged Owner reflects the majority/most-authoritative sourcing; the Waha mention is flagged here rather than silently dropped, and should be re-checked if a future source directly ties this exact pipeline to the Waha JV.

ROUTE: point-to-point only (Zueitina Field 103 → Km91/Line 36B/Brega), no official GIS geometry found for this specific build; RouteAccuracy='low', RouteType='Not mapped (but could be...)'. Did not locate Arabic-language coverage beyond what the English trade press already carries (no additional NOC Arabic-language statement found distinguishing 'Zueitina Field 103' from 'Al-Intisar' — the ambiguity noted above under OWNER remains unresolved by language search).
